picks.name: Power Kitchen
picks.scope: GTA. Kitchen at 46 Hollinger Rd, East York, Toronto, about 10 km from Brimley Rd. Delivers Sunday and Wednesday to about 50 GTA and Southern Ontario locations.
picks.whyPremium: Goal boxes cost $16.22-$26.97 per meal: Keto $16.22-$23.92, Power and Lean Muscle $17.85-$23.95, Pro Athlete $21.77-$26.97 (https://powerkitchen.ca/products.json). There are eight goal plans: Power Meal, Pro Athlete, GLP-1 Support, Low Carb, Clean Bulking, Keto, Lean Muscle and Vegan. A plan-matching quiz asks for goal, exercise level and gender. Plans are auto-renewing subscriptions that can be skipped or paused from a dashboard, including a one-month trial. Delivery is free over $180. It runs loyalty, referral, rewards and ambassador programs (verified on https://powerkitchen.ca/, Oct 16 2026). Menus are nutritionist-designed with printed macros and free consults. Site schema markup claims 4.7 stars from 547 reviews (company claim; not shown in page text).
picks.whyChosen: It is the closest GTA threat to Meal Butler: same fitness audience, family-owned, 10 km away. It proves GTA buyers pay $16-27 a meal for what J&W sells at $8.99-$18.39 (median $12.99 across J&W's pre-set meals, jw-catalog.json). Its quiz, goal plans and skip-or-pause standing order fix J&W's biggest gap: there is no subscription app today, so customers rebuild their carts every week (jw-facts.md). The Shopify audit found no selling plans. Almost all of the play is merchandising on J&W's existing ~292 cooked SKUs, so it can launch fastest. It beats Trifecta (global) for this slot because it is local and price-proven in the same market. J&W already sells Trifecta-style bulk cases.
picks.playIdea: A 60-second quiz asks for goal, weight, training days, dislikes and GLP-1 use. It routes the shopper to one of six J&W plans built only from current Meal Butler SKUs: Lean, Lean Bulk, Athlete, Low Carb/Keto, GLP-1 Companion (3-4oz portions with fibre-rich sides) and Busy Family. Example SKUs include the 4oz/6oz cooked chicken breast in Greek Lemon, Teriyaki, Korean BBQ or Arabic 7 Spice, the 6oz salmon at $11, beef flank fajitas, pre-set meals at $8.99-$14.99, egg bites at $5.25-$5.50, steel-cut oats, broccoli and green beans. Each plan card shows weekly macros, price per meal and two prices: one-off, and Subscribe & Save at 10% off. Customers choose a weekly, biweekly or monthly 'freezer fill'. Frozen vacuum packs make the monthly rhythm possible, which fresh rivals cannot offer. Customers can skip, pause or swap until the Sunday cutoff. A 'Butcher's Pick' default ships a chef-chosen box if the customer does not choose (the Protein Chefs idea). Headline: 'Same macros as Power Kitchen, about 25-45% less per meal, cooked by your butcher.' The 25-45% is an ESTIMATE: $12.99 vs $17.85-$23.95.
picks.revenueLever: Recurring meal-prep revenue at about 40% gross margin after the subscription discount (model-assumptions.md). Benchmark: about $1M a year needs ~320 active biweekly subscribers at C$120 (research/market-benchmarks.md §11). ESTIMATE, year-2 run-rate: 250-350 active subscribers × $120-130 × 26 deliveries ≈ $0.78-1.18M gross. At a 0.8 incrementality factor (some would have ordered anyway) that is about $0.62-0.95M of new revenue. ESTIMATE, year 1 with ramp: $0.35-0.5M. Retention drives the result: standing orders keep 40-55% of customers at month 12, against 15-28% for meal kits (market-benchmarks.md §5a). The plan can be seeded cheaply from J&W's existing customers (Google 4.8 from 611 reviews; Instagram 30K) before paid CAC of C$60-120.

picks.name: Icon Meals (Wholesale program)
picks.scope: Global (Dallas, Texas, USA). Chosen over GTA options because no GTA meal-prep player runs a real wholesale portal.
picks.whyPremium: Icon says it is the 'Official Meal Delivery Service' of the UFC, the US Olympic Team and the Dallas Cowboys (https://iconmeals.com/pages/wholesale). The UFC took an equity stake in 2021, citing 56% annualised growth since 2014 (https://www.ufc.com/news/ufc-announces-major-partnership-icon-meals). It claims a '100% USDA-certified facility' with in-house meat processing and a separate wholesale login. Revenue was over US$14M in 2023 with 75 employees (https://www.garagegymreviews.com/icon-meals-review). It claims 12M+ meals sold (company claim, https://iconmeals.com/).
picks.whyChosen: This model packages J&W's strongest under-used asset. J&W has an Ontario-inspected plant that does its own butchery (since 2008). It holds a 2026 WTO/CPTPP chicken TRQ processor quota (https://www.international.gc.ca/trade-commerce/controls-controles/chicken-poulet/wto_processor-2026-omc_transformateurs.aspx?lang=eng). Its wholesale roots go back to Advance Food Products (1973). Yet it has no wholesale page, tiered pricing or portal (jw-audit.md §5). Icon turned the same capability into a program for 'stores, gyms, weight loss clinics, training centers, offices'. Orders run 'as small as a few dozen meals to weekly shipments of thousands', with an 8-meal minimum. In the GTA, Ultra Fit Mealz and Protein Chefs have only affiliate or partnership pages, so the channel is open. Chosen over My Muscle Chef's 6,000+ stockists because grocery-chain retail needs slotting fees and CPG packaging. Gym and clinic wholesale can start on J&W's existing routes next month.
picks.playIdea: A login-gated B2B portal, using Shopify B2B catalogs and an application form, for six groups: gyms and CrossFit boxes, personal trainers, physio and GLP-1/weight-loss clinics, supplement shops, GTHL/OHL/university teams, and boxing/MMA gyms. It offers tiered case pricing on products J&W already makes: the 4kg chicken breast case ($100 retail), chicken burgers in 25-packs ($35.50 retail), pre-set meals in 12/24/48-meal cases, and egg bites. Partners can add co-branded labels ('Fuelled by J&W at [Gym]'). Terms: a 1-case or 12-meal minimum, net-15 for approved accounts, and standing weekly orders dropped on the existing GTA 1-4 route days. Accounts spending over $300 a week get a loaned J&W reach-in freezer. Every partner also gets a member code that tracks and rewards their members' online orders. Proof points on the sign-up page: Ontario-inspected plant, 30 years of butchery, salt-, sugar- and oil-free cooking, 4.8 Google stars.
picks.revenueLever: A new B2B channel, nearly all incremental, at about 22% gross margin. The margin is lower, but the volume fills plant capacity and makes routes denser (model-assumptions.md). Benchmark: 50 partner gyms × C$400/week ≈ $1.04M a year (market-benchmarks.md §11). Pool: ~2,000 GTA gyms (ESTIMATE), 59 Ontario CrossFit boxes, ~31,460 fitness instructors and trainers in the Toronto region, and 493 GTHL teams (https://gthlcanada.com/article/gthl-announces-team-entries-for-2025-2026-season). ESTIMATE, year-2 run-rate: 35-50 active accounts × $300-400/week × 50 weeks ≈ $0.53-1.0M. Plan on about $0.7M. Member-code referrals add DTC sales on top; those are not counted here.

picks.name: truLOCAL
picks.scope: Canada. Founded in Kitchener, ON in 2016, with warehouses in Ontario, Alberta and BC, and delivery across the GTA. Owned by EMERGE Commerce (TSXV: ECOM) since Jan 2021.
picks.whyPremium: It sells 100% grass-fed and finished beef, organic chicken and wild sockeye from named farms, flash-frozen and vacuum-sealed. Subscription tiers are Starter $155 (up to 36 servings), Family $279 and Mega $349 (https://trulocal.ca/pricing/). Every box carries a 'FREE Meat for Life' item (https://trulocal.ca/free-life/). It claims 70,100+ customers, 511,000+ boxes and 100+ farm partners (company claim, https://trulocal.ca/10-year). Corporate gifting runs in 4 steps with tiered discounts for 10-1,000 gifts (https://trulocal.ca/gifts/). The acquisition was reported at about C$16.8M (https://www.cbc.ca/1.5861576).
picks.whyChosen: truLOCAL is the Ontario default for 'premium meat delivered monthly', and its box is the frozen, vacuum-sealed format J&W already produces. J&W's AAA ribeye works out to about $23-25/lb (10 × 11-12oz for $175). Premium GTA sellers charge $31-60/lb (competitors-gta-meat-grocery.md §2), so J&W can undercut truLOCAL's tiers and still keep margin. truLOCAL is a better model than ButcherBox US because it serves the same customers under the same rules, and it has already translated the 'free meat for life' hook into Canadian prices. The timing is good. Wild Fork's Ontario online service ended Oct 13 2026, and its Whitby, Oakville and Newmarket stores close by Dec 14 2026 (https://retail-insider.com/retail-insider/2026/10/wild-fork-exits-canada-abandoning-ambitious-ontario-expansion-plans/). All three towns are on J&W's Tue/Thu/Fri routes.
picks.playIdea: A raw-meat subscription that ships every 2, 4, 6 or 8 weeks, in three tiers sized by servings. ESTIMATE prices: Starter $129 (~30 servings), Family $229 (~70) and Freezer Fill $299 (~95). Members customise boxes from J&W's raw range: Ontario air-chilled grain-fed chicken, AAA ribeye and striploin, Wagyu striploin and Wagyu/Kobe ground, Ontario lamb chops, pork, wild salmon and bison. The hook is 'a free Meal Butler cooked chicken pack in every box, for life', which gets raw-meat buyers to try the higher-margin cooked line. Product pages show $/lb with a 'J&W vs grocery vs other meat boxes' comparison table. The top tier is productised whole-animal shares: 1/16, 1/8 and 1/4 beef with approximate pounds, a cut sheet and a deposit. These replace the bare '$1,200 quarter cow' listing and sit alongside the $400 Ontario whole lamb. Launch with a 'Welcome, Wild Fork shoppers' landing page and geo-ads in Whitby, Oakville and Newmarket.
picks.revenueLever: Recurring raw-meat revenue and a higher order value, at about 30% gross margin (model-assumptions.md). ESTIMATE run-rate: 250-400 subscribers × $159-229 average box × 11-12 boxes ≈ $0.44-1.1M gross (competitors-gta-meat-grocery.md §5; competitors-global.md §4). At a 0.75 incrementality factor, since some current raw buyers will simply convert, that is about $0.33-0.82M of new revenue. Plan on about $0.6M. 400 subscribers would be ~0.6% of truLOCAL's 70,100-customer base. Wild Fork switchers add about $225K: 150 households × $150/month × 10 months (ESTIMATE, competitors-global.md §4).

picks.name: WeCook (WeCook for Business)
picks.scope: Canada. Montreal-based, founded ~2012. Delivers to Ontario including the GTA, Quebec, New Brunswick and the Halifax area. Ran a Toronto pop-up with Schwartz's in 2025.
picks.whyPremium: Recipes are developed with an executive chef from Joe Beef, and meals are fresh, never frozen. Trustpilot shows 4.8 from 6,584 reviews (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/wecookmeals.ca). WeCook delivers about 90,000 meals a week with nearly 400 employees. On WeCook for Business, the CEO puts the cost at '$11.75-ish' per meal, against $20-25 for traditional catering. Employers can 'contribute $1 per meal, or 100%'. The program suits companies with 20-500 employees, and larger firms get on-site fridges (https://retail-insider.com/?p=177907, verified Oct 16 2026). It has a PK Subban partnership (https://strategyonline.ca/2025/08/26/wecook-pk-subban).
picks.whyChosen: WeCook has the clearest proven Canadian model for employer-paid meals. The employer pays part, the employee pays the rest, and the order goes to one address, which is the cheapest stop on a route. J&W's frozen vacuum-sealed meals suit an unattended office freezer better than WeCook's fresh trays suit a fridge. The Scarborough, Markham, North York and Don Mills business parks are a short drive from Brimley Rd and already on the GTA 2/GTA 4 route days. Chosen over CookUnity/Fraîche smart fridges because the subsidy model needs no hardware to start; a Byte fridge costs about C$7.8-9.9K plus C$177/month (https://www.bytetechnology.co/pricing). This is a separate buyer from pick #2. Here the employer funds an employee benefit; in #2, gyms and clinics buy to resell.
picks.playIdea: A workplace meal-benefit portal for GTA employers: offices, hospitals and clinics, logistics warehouses, manufacturing plants and property managers. The employer sets a subsidy, from $2 a meal to 100%. Employees pre-order Meal Butler pre-set meals, protein bowls, egg bites and oats at a staff price of about $11-13 by Sunday. J&W delivers the orders in bulk to one dock on the Wednesday or Friday route. Sites with 75+ staff get a loaned J&W freezer restocked weekly as a 'healthy vending' replacement, paid by tap or payroll billing. A team-lunch catering tray menu uses the same proteins and sides. HR gets wellness add-ons: a monthly lunch-and-learn with J&W's nutrition coach and a step-challenge prize of a Meal Butler week.
picks.revenueLever: A new B2B corporate channel. Cooked meals delivered in bulk to one stop earn about 35-45% gross margin (model-assumptions.md). Pool: ~11-14K GTA locations with 50+ staff (ESTIMATE from StatCan counts, https://yorklink.ca/2025-york-region-business-counts-factsheet/) and ~810K Toronto office jobs, with hybrid staff on site ~3 days (https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/97af-CityPlanning-Toronto-Employment-Survey-Two-Pager-Summary-2025.pdf). Benchmark: 40 offices × 25 staff × 2 meals/week × $13 × 48 weeks ≈ $1.25M (market-benchmarks.md §11). ESTIMATE, year-2 run-rate: 15-30 workplaces × 40-60 meals/week × $12 × 48 weeks ≈ $0.35-1.04M. Plan on about $0.6M. The sales cycle is slower than gyms, so year 1 is about $0.2-0.3M.

picks.name: Omaha Steaks (Business Gifts)
picks.scope: Global (Omaha, Nebraska, USA). Chosen over GTA gifting players (Pusateri's, McEwan) because it is the clearly better B2B gifting machine.
picks.whyPremium: Omaha Steaks is a heritage premium steak brand with a dedicated business-gifting arm. It claims 5,000+ business clients since 2020, 350,000+ custom gift certificates and 700,000+ coolers delivered to business recipients (company claims, https://www.omahasteaks.com/business-gifts?SRC=RZ0636; that page returned 403 on re-check, so the figures come from earlier research). 'Choice' gift certificates carry a company logo, a personal message and volume pricing at bands from under 10 to 500+ recipients. Recipients pick their own steaks, seafood or sides and redeem online, by phone or by mail (verified at https://business.omahasteaks.com/resources/corporate-gift-certificates).
picks.whyChosen: Corporate gifting is the only play that can bring in cash this quarter, in the Q4 2026 holiday season. Omaha's 'Choice' certificate also solves J&W's real constraint: perishable boxes and unknown recipient addresses. A certificate lets each employee or client pick a box and book delivery on J&W's routes, or pick up at Brimley Rd. J&W already has the boxes: Gentleman's Box $129.99, A Taste of Greece $130, Long Weekend $199, Girls Night $89.99, Ultimate BBQ Dad Pack $84.99, plus gift cards (jw-catalog.json). It has no corporate program, though (jw-facts.md). GTA alternatives are consumer gift ladders or small-scale flows: Pusateri's $64.99-$349.99 boxes and truLOCAL's 4-step upload.
picks.playIdea: A self-serve corporate gifting page built around four tiers. Approximate gift values: $85 (BBQ Dad Pack), $130 (Gentleman's Box or Taste of Greece, which plays to Greek-Canadian heritage and J&W's 154 Mediterranean SKUs), $200 (Long Weekend) and $350 (a new 'J&W Reserve' Wagyu and AAA striploin box). The buyer adds a logo and message, uploads a recipient CSV, and picks one of two fulfilment options. The first is direct delivery on GTA routes or Ontario long-haul. The second is a branded 'J&W Choice' e-certificate the recipient redeems for any box, a Butcher Club month or a Meal Butler week. Volume discounts start at 10, 50, 100 and 500 recipients, and buyers can pay by invoice. An occasion-reminder engine covers year-end, Greek Easter, client thank-yous, realtor closings and employee milestones. Every tier stays under the CRA $500 non-cash gift cap (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/benefits-allowances/gifts-awards-social-events/gifts-awards-long-service-awards.html).
picks.revenueLever: Seasonal, high-margin B2B revenue at about 40% gross margin, plus new customers: every redemption captures an email for the welcome flow. ESTIMATE: a conservative case of 60 companies × 25 gifts × $130 ≈ $195K (competitors-gta-meat-grocery.md §5). An upside case of ~115 firms (1% of ~11-14K GTA locations with 50+ staff) × 60 boxes × $120 ≈ $830K (market-benchmarks.md §11). Plan on $0.25-0.4M a year, about 60% of it in Nov-Dec. No current Canadian per-employee gifting figure was found; the $50-150 per box range is an ESTIMATE.

picks.name: Calo
picks.scope: Global (Riyadh, GCC; UK through its 2025 acquisitions of Fresh Fitness Food and Detox Kitchen). Chosen over GTA personalisation (One Life Meals' InBody scans, Meels' calculator) as clearly the better model; One Life's scan idea is folded into the play.
picks.whyPremium: Calo reports 'high-growth nine-figure' (US$) annualised revenue, 50%+ year-on-year growth in H1 2025, a US$64M Series B, 10M+ meals in a year, and 10+ physical sites including hospital-based outlets (https://www.wamda.com/2025/07/calo-raises-39-milliion-series-b-extension-boost-global-growth, verified Oct 16 2026). It also claims 280K GCC customers and 18M meals delivered (company claim, https://calo.app/en-sa). Its Custom Macros plan takes the customer's own targets, and customers can pause, skip or edit up to 48h before delivery. It is piloting 'Calo Black', an LLM private chef that learns preferences through conversation and generates personalised daily menus. It partners with premium gym operator Armah Sports.
picks.whyChosen: Personalisation turns J&W's sprawling à la carte catalogue into a premium, guided experience. The catalogue has 979 products and ~292 cooked items, and 51% of products have empty descriptions (jw-facts.md). The play also ties directly to the AI-agents section of the proposal. No GTA rival goes beyond a static quiz (Power Kitchen) or a calculator (Meels). J&W already weighs every portion, so a personal-macro label costs little to add. Ranked below the channel plays because part of its revenue overlaps with pick #1. It works mainly as a premium tier and a conversion engine.
picks.playIdea: A chat concierge on jwfoods.com and in Instagram DMs, the 30K-follower channel. It asks for goal, height and weight, training schedule, dislikes, budget and GLP-1 use, then calculates daily macros. It builds a ready-to-buy weekly cart from Meal Butler SKUs to hit those macros, for example 6oz Greek Lemon chicken with rice and broccoli for lunch, and egg bites with steel-cut oats for breakfast. It explains swaps and converts the cart into a standing order in one tap. A premium 'Personal Macro Plan' tier has a set weekly price, portions weighed to the customer's own grams and the customer's name on each label (the Fresh Fitness Food model). A $25 InBody scan at the Brimley Rd store every 4 weeks (the One Life Meals idea, https://www.onelifemeals.com/) feeds an automatic re-plan. A human fallback, Lucas, Tasia or a partner dietitian, offers a free 15-minute call.
picks.revenueLever: Conversion, order value and a premium tier, at about 45% gross margin on cooked food (model-assumptions.md). ESTIMATE: 40-80 Personal Macro Plan clients × ~$180/week × 40 active weeks ≈ $0.29-0.58M gross, plus an assumed +5-10% conversion and order-value lift on AI-guided online orders (ESTIMATE, not a vendor claim). After a 0.8 incrementality factor, and removing overlap with the Goal Plan Builder, plan on about $0.25-0.45M of net new revenue. Build cost is low because it reuses the existing catalogue and Shopify.

picks.name: Halenda's Meats (Halenda's Fundraising)
picks.scope: GTA (Durham Region). Head office at 915 Nelson St, Oshawa. Five GTA/Durham stores including Whitby, plus St Jacobs Market; the site claims 2 processing plants. A direct competitor on J&W's Tuesday Durham route.
picks.whyPremium: Halenda's makes award-winning smoked meats: the 2026 Diamond Award plus six more at Ontario's Finest Meat Competition. It runs a full-service custom-cut counter and an Iberico-style line. Its charcuterie is listed in select Metro, Sobeys, Foodland, Food Basics and Fortinos stores (https://www.halendas.com/). Named 'Hibernator' freezer packs cost $199, $299 and $349 (https://www.halendas.com/products/meat-freezer-packs/). The fundraising program says it has helped groups raise 'more than six million dollars', tied to six million meat sticks sold. It serves schools, hockey, baseball, ringette, soccer, scouts, cadets and United Way, promising 'less selling and less administration' (https://halendasfundraising.com/, verified Oct 16 2026).
picks.whyChosen: Halenda's is the closest local analogue to J&W: a family butcher with its own processing. Its fundraising engine is a proven way to put product into thousands of new households at near-zero CAC. J&W has a stronger story for sports parents (high-protein, no salt, sugar or oil added). The GTHL alone has 493 teams and 30,000+ participants (https://gthlcanada.com/article/gthl-announces-team-entries-for-2025-2026-season). Chosen for the community slot over Sanagan's Meat Club points and Mama Earth's paid Earth Perks membership because those mainly re-reward existing customers, while this brings in new ones. It is also more proven than Rowe Farms' youth fundraisers, though Rowe's 'donation shown under each price' UX is borrowed.
picks.playIdea: A fundraiser storefront. Each school, GTHL or minor hockey team, soccer club, cadet corps or church group gets its own page, share link and live progress bar. Families order J&W bundles: a Team Freezer Pack (chicken burgers 25-pack, 4kg chicken breast case, ground beef), a Meal Butler 'game-week' pack, and a new J&W-made chicken or beef jerky or protein stick from the inspected plant. The group's donation is shown under each price, Rowe Farms-style. J&W aggregates the orders and delivers them in one drop to the school or arena on the existing route day, or customers pick up at Brimley Rd. Every buyer gets an opt-in Meal Butler welcome offer, and the coach gets a free team-nutrition talk. Launch with the winter hockey season and spring soccer.
picks.revenueLever: New-customer acquisition plus seasonal volume. Contribution is thinner after the 15-20% given to groups (ESTIMATE), so this is mainly an acquisition channel. ESTIMATE: 40 groups × $3,000 ≈ $120K in year 1 (competitors-gta-meat-grocery.md §5), scaling to 100 groups × $4,000 ≈ $400K in year 2. Follow-on DTC: if 10% of an estimated 3,000-6,000 buyer households become $130 repeat customers ordering 4 times a year, that adds ≈ $0.16-0.31M (ESTIMATE). Plan on about $0.25-0.5M total. Halenda's program timeframe and group count were not found, so its $6M figure is used only as proof of the model, not for sizing.

rationale:
Each pick fills a different one of the seven slots the brief asked for:
1. Meal-prep subscription and builder: Power Kitchen.
2. B2B wholesale to gyms, clinics and teams: Icon Meals.
3. Raw premium meat and whole-animal boxes: truLOCAL.
4. Corporate employee-meal benefit: WeCook for Business.
5. Corporate gifting: Omaha Steaks.
6. Personalised nutrition with AI: Calo.
7. Community fundraising: Halenda's.

The two B2B picks are kept apart by buyer. In #2, gyms and clinics buy wholesale to resell. In #4, an employer funds meals as a staff benefit.

Scope, stated honestly:
- GTA-headquartered: Power Kitchen (East York) and Halenda's (Oshawa, Durham).
- Canadian operators that sell into the GTA: truLOCAL (Kitchener, ON) and WeCook (Montreal; delivers in Ontario).
- Global: Icon Meals, Omaha Steaks and Calo.

That is 4 GTA/Canada and 3 global. A global operator replaced a GTA one only where no GTA player runs the model at real scale. No GTA meal-prep company has a working wholesale portal. GTA gifting is consumer-grade (Pusateri's, McEwan). GTA personalisation stops at a quiz (Power Kitchen) or a calculator (Meels).

Ranking logic: each play's run-rate revenue for J&W, multiplied by how much of it is new, multiplied by how fast it can start. All are ESTIMATES built from research/model-assumptions.md and market-benchmarks.md, with the competitor URLs cited in each pick.

Year-2 planning midpoints:

| Rank | Play | Midpoint |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Goal Plan Builder | ~$0.8M |
| 2 | Pro Partner Portal | ~$0.7M |
| 3 | Butcher Club | ~$0.6M, plus Wild Fork switchers |
| 4 | J&W at Work | ~$0.6M |
| 5 | Corporate Gift Studio | ~$0.3M, but the fastest cash because Q4 is now |
| 6 | AI Coach | ~$0.35M, partly overlapping #1 |
| 7 | Team Fuel Fundraiser | ~$0.3M, mainly acquisition |

Together that is about $3.6M gross if everything worked. The +$1M target (about +40% on the ~$2.5M mid-case baseline) therefore needs only the top 2-3 plays at midpoint, or roughly 30% of the full set. That leaves room for misses.

Margin is not the same across plays:
- Cooked meals: about 40-45% gross.
- Gifting: about 40%.
- Raw meat: about 30%.
- Wholesale: about 22%.

So #1, #4, #5 and #6 are worth more per dollar than #2 and #3.

Regulatory caveat: J&W is provincially inspected (Ontario, since 2008). All seven plays are designed to sell inside Ontario on J&W's existing GTA and long-haul routes. Icon's national wholesale and Omaha's national shipping cannot be copied outside Ontario without a federal SFCR licence.

Two timing tailwinds were verified:
- Wild Fork's Ontario online service ended Oct 13 2026. Its Whitby, Oakville and Newmarket stores, all on J&W routes, close by Dec 14 2026 (Retail Insider). This feeds play #3.
- Goodfood is distressed and LiveFit has closed, which frees up their customers for play #1.

Figures re-checked live on Oct 16 2026: Power Kitchen's plans and features, Icon's wholesale terms, Halenda's $6M+ fundraising claim, WeCook for Business pricing and subsidy, Calo's funding, growth and Calo Black, and Omaha's Choice certificate mechanics. The Omaha client and cooler counts come from the earlier research pass, because that page returned 403 on re-check.

Excluded: LiveFit Foods (closed), Superfit Foods (domain for sale), Cumbrae's (no working e-commerce), and Organic Garage, Vince's Market and Healthy Planet (could not be verified as operating).
alsoConsidered: Trifecta Nutrition (global, US$100M+ run-rate): the closest product match, with bulk cooked protein by the lb plus a macro app. Lost slot 1 to Power Kitchen, which is local and price-proven in the GTA. J&W already sells bulk cases, and the macro-app idea feeds the Calo play.
My Muscle Chef (global, A$200M, 6,000+ stockists): the best retail/CPG model, but a later stage. Grocery-chain slotting and CPG packaging come after the Pro Partner Portal proves demand.

ButcherBox US (US$570M+, ~450K subscribers) and ButcherBox.ca (Mississauga hub, own reefer trucks): good subscription-meat benchmarks. truLOCAL was chosen because it is Ontario-based and already priced in CAD.
CookUnity / Fraîche smart fridges (Toronto since June 2025): strong office-fridge model, but it needs ~C$7.8-9.9K of hardware per fridge. Kept as phase 2 of J&W at Work.
Rowe Farms and VG Meats (Harvest to Gather): premium GTA whole-animal shares (1/16 to 1/2 beef with weights) and youth fundraisers. Their ideas are folded into Butcher Club and Team Fuel.
Sanagan's Meat Locker (Toronto Life's 'best butcher'): Meat Club points with a weekly 3X item. Folded into the Butcher Club retention mechanics. A retention lever, not a new-revenue channel.
Mama Earth / The Healthy Butcher: Earth Perks paid membership. A 'Butler Pass' that removes the route fee is a good add-on, but a smaller revenue lever.
Pusateri's Fine Foods: luxury gift-box ladder ($64.99-$349.99) and $/lb display. Lost the gifting slot to Omaha's B2B Choice-certificate model.
Hi Chef: the luxury ceiling ($26-$30 entrées) and an Early Bird discount. Useful for price anchoring, but not a distinct revenue play.
OTR Meals: discounted prepaid gift-card bundles for affinity groups (likely TPS). A strong add-on to the Corporate Gift Studio.
Protein Chefs ('we choose for you' default), Thryve (macro-app barcodes) and MealFix (Protein Plus upsell): tactics folded into the Goal Plan Builder.
Factor Canada: free dietitian consult and a GLP-1 line. Folded into the GLP-1 Companion plan and the AI Coach.
Wild Fork (JBS) exiting Ontario: a campaign opportunity used in Butcher Club, not a model to copy.

Excluded: LiveFit Foods (closed), Goodfood (distressed, but a source of switching customers), Superfit Foods (inactive), Cumbrae's (no e-commerce), and Organic Garage, Vince's Market and Healthy Planet (could not be verified).
